title: agentrc Resolved Manifest
description: The resolved resource manifest produced when an Agentfile is compiled to an OCI artifact. Records the exact bases, resources, SOP, and secret references that the build resolved, so a build is reproducible and a platform can audit what was embedded versus fetched at runtime.

build_id.description: Opaque identifier for the build that produced this manifest.

agentfile_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the Agentfile source that was compiled.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the build resolved this manifest.

policy_mode.description: How POLICY requests were encoded into labels: inline values in labels, or a digest of a structured manifest layer (see spec --policy-mode).

labels_digest.description: Digest over the emitted org.agentrc.* label set, for integrity checks.

base.description: The resolved FROM base image or parent agent.

ref.description: The FROM reference as authored (image or parent agent).

digest.description: Content-addressed digest the ref resolved to.

resources.description: Resolved tools, skills, and MCP servers added via COPY (local) or ADD --remote, keyed by their /mnt destination.

kind.description: Resource type, determined by the destination path under /mnt.

delivery.description: How the resource was delivered: local COPY, fetched and embedded at build (cached), or referenced and fetched at bootstrap (runtime).

digest.description: Resolved content digest for embedded resources (org.agentrc.<kind>.<name>).

origin.description: Origin reference (org.agentrc.<kind>.<name>.origin) so a platform may re-point to a mirror without rebuilding.

fail_mode.description: Behaviour if the resource cannot be resolved: abort, or warn and continue.

sop.description: The resolved SOP embedded at /mnt/SOP (pointer + digest, never the full text).

sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the SOP file embedded at /mnt/SOP (org.agentrc.sop.sha256).

secrets.description: Secret references declared via LABEL org.agentrc.secret.<name>=<scope>. Values are never recorded here; the platform broker resolves them at run time.
